record.original_question: For every log-concave probability measure μ on R^n with covariance matrix A, does there exist a universal constant C > 0 such that the isoperimetric constant ψ_μ is bounded below by C / √(||A||_{op})? Equivalently, up to a universal constant, is the minimal boundary measure always attained by a half-space, as predicted by the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$, i.e. a Borel probability measure whose density $f$ with respect to Lebesgue measure (when restricted to its support) satisfies $f(\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y) \ge f(x)^\lambda f(y)^{1-\lambda}$ for all $x,y$ in the support and $\lambda \in [0,1]$. Assume $\mu$ has finite second moments and let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ denote its covariance matrix, with operator norm $\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. The isoperimetric (Cheeger) constant of $\mu$ is defined by
$$\psi_\mu \;=\; \inf_{S \subset \mathbb{R}^n} \frac{\mu^+(\partial S)}{\min(\mu(S), 1-\mu(S))},$$
where the infimum runs over all Borel sets $S$ and $\mu^+(\partial S) = \liminf_{\varepsilon \to 0^+}\frac{\mu(S_\varepsilon)-\mu(S)}{\varepsilon}$ is the Minkowski boundary measure (with $S_\varepsilon$ the open $\varepsilon$-neighborhood of $S$).

Prove or disprove: there exists a universal constant $C>0$, independent of $n$ and of $\mu$, such that for every log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\psi_\mu \;\ge\; \frac{C}{\sqrt{\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}}}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The full KLS conjecture remains open as of 2025. Major related conjectures—Bourgain's slicing problem and the thin-shell conjecture—were resolved by Klartag and Lehec (2024–2025), building on a small-ball technique of Guan. Their thin-shell bound yields the current best (polylogarithmic) lower bound on $\psi_\mu$, but does not establish the conjectured universal constant.
